ebitda_multiple_valuation.multiple_justification: The lowest end of the sector range is applied due to extreme customer concentration (88%), a 49% revenue decline in the most recent year, and the fact that adjusted EBITDA is negative when accounting for market-rate management costs.
premium_factors_applied: High historical margins during peak project years
discount_factors_applied: Extreme customer concentration (88.31% from one client)

sensitivity.key_customer_loss_impact: Loss of Client 1 would result in an 88% revenue drop, rendering the business insolvent and reducing value to net cash after liquidation costs.

seller_anchor_points: Historical high margins (50% operating margin in 2025)
seller_expectations.negotiation_gap_assessment: Significant. The seller will likely anchor on the 2025 'outlier' year and the cash balance, whereas a buyer will focus on the negative adjusted EBITDA and the 88% client concentration risk.

key_findings: The business is technically worth more as a collection of assets (cash) than as a going concern due to negative adjusted EBITDA.
Adjusted EBITDA is negative (£-5,526) once a market-rate salary for a replacement manager is factored in.
The 88.31% revenue concentration in a single client makes the earnings stream highly speculative.
The company has a strong cash position of £195,634 (from 2026 Operational Assessment) but owes £149,587.37 to directors.
Revenue volatility is extreme, with a 49% decline in the most recent year.
red_flags: Significant director loan liability (£149k) to be settled.
narrative: Valuing Cooper Gibson as a going concern using an EBITDA multiple is problematic because the 'Base Case' adjusted EBITDA is negative (£-5,526) after normalizing director compensation. While the company reported a 2026 EBITDA of £57,012, this relies on an under-market director salary of £12,570. A commercial buyer must account for the £44,930 cost to replace the owner-manager. Consequently, the Enterprise Value is effectively zero under standard earnings methodologies. The primary value of the business lies in its Net Assets, specifically the cash balance of £195,634 (as cited in the 2026 Operational Assessment). However, this is offset by a substantial liability of £149,587.37 owed to directors (Risk Expert, 2026-06-25). The resulting Equity Value is heavily dependent on whether the buyer views the remaining client relationship as sustainable. Given the 88% concentration risk, any deal should be structured with a low upfront payment and a significant earn-out. The Net Asset Value of £183,083 serves as the absolute ceiling for valuation, though a buyer is unlikely to pay full NAV for a business with negative adjusted earnings and extreme concentration risk.
